To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SDN data collection mechanisms provide the ability to collect a variety of traffic related data and that ML techniques are able to classify traffic with good accuracy using this data.

the SDN architecture is an excellent platform for the implementation of ML applications, that the data collected by SDNs can be used for ML applications, that supervised learning is a suitable ML technique for traffic classification, that the data sets obtained are suitable for ML applications, and that high classification accuracy can be achieved.
we have developed an OpenFlow based architecture that collects traffic data and we have used the data to perform traffic classification using ML techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of ML techniques in SDNs and the data collection mechanisms of OpenFlow.
the application of machine learning in Software Defined Networks (ML-SDN) and in particular the use of data-sets obtained using the OpenFlow data collection mechanism.

the following questions: (1) what type of information can be obtained from SDN data-sets, (2) how can ML be used to extract that information, and (3) how can the information be used to control the network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SDNs are a promising platform for the development of ML applications in networks.
ML can be used to classify network traffic in SDNs with high accuracy.

SDNs provide a rich set of tools for ML applications, but that the ML community needs to work together with the SDN community to make the data collection and processing more efficient and to provide a standard way to access the data for ML applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OpenFlow protocol is an excellent tool to implement network control applications based on ML.
we have shown that it is feasible to use ML in SDNs and that the data-sets obtained can be used to train ML classifiers to perform traffic classification.
we show how to gather network traffic data in a software defined network, and how to use that data for network control applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the data collected in SDNs can be used to implement ML applications that can learn from network traffic and improve network control and management.
the data-sets obtained from SDNs can be used for ML applications.
the data collected in SDNs is suitable for ML applications.
